subject: general
question: Select the correct statement.

options.text: Jawaharlal Nehru was the first deputy chairman of the planning commission.
The Second Five-Year Plan was based on the PC Mahalanobis model.
The Second Five-Year Plan was based on the Russian model introduced by Joseph Stalin.
The First Five-Year Plan was based on the PC Mahalanobis model.

solution:
The correct answer is __**The Second Five-Year Plan was based on the PC Mahalanobis model.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The duration of the second five-year plan was 1956–61__.
 
• The five-year plans were one of the central plans.
 
• The plans were formulated and were financed by the central government.
 
• These were launched in 1951, with fist five-year plans covering the years 1951-56.
 
• There were three breaks in five-year plans during 1966-69, 1978-80, and 1991-92.
 
• During 1966-69, consequences of war, drought, and a misbalanced economy lead to the abandonment of a five-year plan and three annual plans were launched.
 
• The breaks of 1978-80 and 19991-92 were due to a change of government and economic crisis respectively.

Main objectives of the second five-year plan:

__
 
• It was also called Mahalanobis Plan after the name of its architect.
 
• Rapid industrialization was the main objective of this plan.
 
• Imports were encouraged that later led to the emptying of forex reserves.
 
• The Agricultural sector was not given much importance.
 
• As a result of all this Shortage of food, the increased price of goods and capital shortage was observed.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Planning Commission

 
 
• The Planning Commission, although no longer active (since it was replaced by the NITI Aayog), was an important feature of policymaking and governance in India.
 
• The Planning Commission was reporting directly to the Prime Minister of India.
 
• The Planning Commission was established in March 1950 by an executive resolution of the Government of India, on the recommendation of the Advisory Planning Board constituted in 1946, under the chairman of KC Neogi. Thus the Planning Commission was neither constitutional nor a statutory body. It was an advisory body. 
 
• It is a non-constitutional (not created by the Constitution) and a non-statutory body (not created by an act of Parliament).
 
• In India, it was the supreme organ of planning for social and economic development.
 
• It was not responsible for making and implementing decisions.
 
• This responsibility rests with the Central and State governments.
 
• The Planning Commission was only a staff agency- an advisory body and has no executive responsibility.
 
• The critics have described it as a 'Super Cabinet', an 'Economic Cabinet' a 'Parallel Cabinet', the 'Fifth Wheel of the Coach' etc.
